Purpose and exclusions

Projectile ability AimedArrow

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Create DA_Ability_Ranger_AimedArrow with the listed actual asset/service type at the planned path, after its prerequisites are ready.
  2. Populate the listed required fields and validate identities/references before assigning the asset into the named phase consumer.
  3. Run its concrete fixture and reject missing/incompatible configuration; a named file alone has no gameplay effect.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Author and validate stable definition/frame/field identity before use; load through declared references at readiness.
  2. Consumers may cache read-only references for their world/session lifetime; do not mutate the shared definition or place player quantities on it.
  3. On reimport/version change validate compatibility and migrate persistent IDs deliberately. Missing required rules fail closed; missing cosmetic layers use documented fallback.
  4. World/pawn teardown releases runtime references; persistent records retain IDs and versions only. Reconnect resolves the same definition without replaying grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Melee sweeps, server projectiles and hit deduplication. Rule owner: URPGHitResolver. This asset’s role is Projectile ability AimedArrow

  1. GAS accepts the ability and creates one hit execution with a gameplay time interval and accepted stats/context.
  2. Server advances windup/active/recovery on its own clock. If a frame crosses the complete active interval, perform the bounded swept query for the crossed segment instead of losing the hit window.
  3. Normalize overlap/trace results to target actors, check collision/LOS/faction and insert target identity into AttemptedTargetIds before invoking damage.
  4. For ranged attacks, spawn a server-owned projectile with collision and movement, ignore the instigator and resolve blocking impact once; clients may predict a cosmetic projectile that is reconciled to the accepted one.
  5. Damage/healing effects apply through the one GAS effect path. Cosmetic PaperZD notifies may add sounds but cannot call ResolveImpact or release authoritative cooldowns.
  6. Cancel execution on death/interruption/invalid avatar and destroy or invalidate remaining projectiles under their authored lifetime policy.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_NetworkLab / Dummy_Near / Dummy_Far / ProjectileWall. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Two components on one target overlap -> one damage attempt per execution.
Packet replay or duplicated overlap -> AlreadyAttempted, no extra damage.
Projectile hits wall before enemy -> destroyed/blocked; no damage through wall.
Attacker dies in windup -> Canceled; missed animation completion cannot leave a permanent attack lock.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not put mutable stock, current health, inventory quantities or player quest progress on a shared Data Asset. A soft reference still needs validation and readiness.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
